fixes.explanation: Friends and money aren't on Paul's list, baker. He points to his teaching, his conduct, his purpose, his faith, his patience, his love and his perseverance (2 Timothy 3:10). You won't find a paycheck anywhere in that list. Every item is about Paul himself.

Nice guess, but Paul never mentions a family or a home in this list. What he says Timothy observed is his teaching, his conduct, his purpose, his faith and more (2 Timothy 3:10). Those are things about Paul himself. It's a bit like watching how somebody handles a burnt batch instead of touring their kitchen.

Paul doesn't say the towns welcomed him. What he says is that the Lord rescued him from all of those persecutions (2 Timothy 3:11). The rescue he names comes from the Lord. Antioch, Iconium and Lystra get no welcome mat in that verse.

Paul says it straight: "Indeed, all who desire to live godly lives in Christ Jesus will be persecuted…" (2 Timothy 3:12). He just walked through his own stories, so he isn't guessing. It's not exactly a recruiting slogan, is it? But Paul tells Timothy the truth, and the verse right before it says the Lord rescued Paul from all of it (2 Timothy 3:11).

Wouldn't that be nice? A round of applause for living godly. But Paul says all who desire to live godly lives in Christ Jesus will be persecuted (2 Timothy 3:12). Paul had just reminded Timothy of his own persecutions and sufferings (2 Timothy 3:11). He wants him to know that ahead of time.

That's the line: "…evil men and imposters go from bad to worse…" (2 Timothy 3:13). An imposter doesn't get better by pretending longer. The direction Paul describes is downhill. It's like a cookie batch that gets a little more burnt every time it goes back in the oven.
Paul says the opposite, baker. Evil men and imposters "…go from bad to worse…" (2 Timothy 3:13). Wiser would be going up, and Paul describes going down. Nothing in that verse says they get any wiser.

Paul gives the reason right in the verse: "…since you know from whom you have learned them." (2 Timothy 3:14) Timothy knows the source of what he learned. That's the reason Paul gives. Timothy can trust it because he knows who taught him.

Not quite, friend. Paul says, "From infancy you have known the Holy Scriptures…" (2 Timothy 3:15). So Timothy's time with the Scriptures goes back to infancy. The statement said he first knew them after meeting Paul, and the verse doesn't say that.

You got it. Paul says, "From infancy you have known the Holy Scriptures…" (2 Timothy 3:15). So Timothy's time with the Scriptures started in infancy, not at some later point. That's what makes the statement False.

Yes, faith. Paul says the Holy Scriptures "…are able to make you wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus." (2 Timothy 3:15) The Scriptures make Timothy wise for salvation, and that comes through faith in Christ Jesus. It's a short word carrying a big load.

Paul points higher than that. He says, "All Scripture is God-breathed…" (2 Timothy 3:16). God is the source he names, not a line of elders. Elders aren't in that verse at all. This verse says it came from God's breath.
No committee meeting in this verse, friend. Paul says, "All Scripture is God-breathed…" (2 Timothy 3:16). The source he names is God, and he says ALL Scripture. Scholars don't come up in that verse.
